section_summary: This section (pages 414-453) concludes a State Department research compilation on Japanese cultural and natural monuments, followed by diplomatic correspondence and memoranda from 1948 to 1949 regarding Japanese territorial boundaries. It includes an official Japanese list of protected historic sites, scenic spots, and natural preserves, an airgram on Kagoshima's desire to reincorporate the Ryukyu Islands below 30°N, a Korean petition claiming sovereignty over Dokdo (Liancourt Rocks), Tsushima, and Parang Island, and a report on postwar conditions and reconstruction in Hiroshima. The final documents consist of government and corporate inquiries and legal memoranda concerning the international boundary of Japan and whether the legal definition of Japanese territory includes Okinawa.

subfiles.about: Lists Japanese protected historic sites, scenic spots, and natural preserves across multiple prefectures, along with removals and source references.
subfiles.summary: This concluding excerpt of a reference report catalogues officially designated Japanese historic sites, scenic spots, and natural monuments in western Japan and across prefectural boundaries. It details botanical, zoological, geological, and historical assets, designations without limiting area, and monuments removed from protection through December 1944.
subfiles.title: Catalogue of Japanese Historic Sites, Scenic Spots, and Natural Monuments (R-231-CR-B-1 Excerpt)

subfiles.about: Reports the Kagoshima Vice Governor's request for the return of islands below 30 degrees north latitude in the peace treaty.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports the Kagoshima Vice Governor's appeal to restore islands south of 30°N, including Amami Oshima, to Japan.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-123 on Territorial Claims of Kagoshima Prefecture Below 30 Degrees North Latitude

subfiles.about: Transmits a petition from the Patriotic Old Men's Association of Seoul claiming several islands for Korea.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a Seoul petition claiming Korean sovereignty over Dokdo (Liancourt Rocks), Ulleungdo, Tsushima, and Parang Island.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 612 Transmitting Korean Petition on Island Sovereignty

subfiles.about: Petitions SCAP for the transfer of Dokdo, Tsushima, and Parang Island to Korea in the postwar settlement.
subfiles.from: Cho Sung-whan, Chairman, Patriotic Old Men's Association, Seoul, Korea
subfiles.summary: The Patriotic Old Men's Association petitions General MacArthur to award Dokdo (Liancourt Rocks), Tsushima, and Parang Island to Korea in the peace settlement. It sets forth historical, geographical, economic, and security arguments asserting Korean ownership and claims Japan used these islands as staging points for continental aggression.
subfiles.title: Petition to General MacArthur Requesting Land Arrangements Between Korea and Japan
subfiles.to: General Douglas MacArthur, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum by Foreign Service Officer Richard B. Finn reporting on his visit to Hiroshima.
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Counselor of Mission, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Richard B. Finn's report detailing postwar reconstruction, economic conditions, and civic attitudes in Hiroshima.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 251 Transmitting Summary 'Impressions of Hiroshima'

subfiles.about: Surveys physical rebuilding, industrial activity, atomic bomb casualty research, and civic perspectives in Hiroshima.
subfiles.from: Richard B. Finn, Foreign Service Officer
subfiles.summary: Richard B. Finn describes his visit to Hiroshima, reviewing rebuilding efforts, operations at Toyo Kogyo, research by the Atomic Bomb Casualty Commission, local recollections of the bombing, and discussions with Mayor Shinzo Hamai regarding finances and occupation administration.
subfiles.title: Impressions of Hiroshima
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Inquires about the newly established international boundaries of Japan between Formosa and to the north.
subfiles.from: Secretary, Department of Geography, University of California, Berkeley
subfiles.summary: Requests information on the new international boundaries of Japan, specifically points between Formosa and northward.
subfiles.title: Inquiry from University of California Department of Geography Regarding Japan's Boundaries

subfiles.about: Explains that Japan's boundaries cannot be defined until a peace treaty is negotiated.
subfiles.summary: States that because the Japanese peace treaty has not been negotiated, new international boundaries cannot yet be specified.
subfiles.title: State Department Reply Concerning Japan's International Boundaries
subfiles.to: Mrs. Miller, Department of Geography, University of California, Berkeley

subfiles.about: Provides legal advice on whether 'territory of Japan' includes Okinawa under military occupation.
subfiles.from: Conrad E. Snow, L/P, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Advises that Okinawa was internationally recognized Japanese territory before the war and remains under U.S. military occupation.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on Eastern United Company Inquiry Concerning Okinawa and Japanese Territory
subfiles.to: Noel Hemmendinger, NA, Department of State

subfiles.about: Requests a legal opinion to formulate a reply to the Eastern United Company inquiry.
subfiles.from: Noel Hemmendinger, NA, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Asks H.F.F. for an opinion to serve as the basis for answering the Eastern United Company letter.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Routing Note Requesting Legal Opinion on Eastern United Company Letter

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the contractual phrase 'territory of Japan' legally encompasses Okinawa for a construction franchise.
subfiles.from: C. A. Blum, President, Eastern United Company, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether 'territory of Japan' legally includes Okinawa for an exclusive Airform Construction franchise.
subfiles.title: Letter from Eastern United Company to State Department Regarding Okinawa Territory Status
subfiles.to: John M. Allison, Department of State

subfiles.about: Refers Eastern United Company's inquiry regarding the legal definition of Japan to the State Department for direct reply.
subfiles.from: Ada V. Espenshade (for Michael Lee), Far Eastern Branch, Office of International Trade, Department of Commerce
subfiles.summary: Transmits Eastern United Company's inquiry regarding the legal definition of Japan to the State Department for direct response.
subfiles.title: Commerce Department Transmittal of Eastern United Company Inquiry to State Department
subfiles.to: Noel Hemmendinger, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the term 'territory of Japan' includes Okinawa in connection with its Airform Construction franchise.
subfiles.from: C. A. Blum, President, Eastern United Company, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification from Commerce whether Okinawa legally constitutes Japanese territory under an Airform Construction license.
subfiles.title: Letter from Eastern United Company to Commerce Department Regarding Status of Okinawa
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Division, Office of International Trade, U.S. Department of Commerce
